diagnostic_evidence.quote: A strictly monotonically increasing and differentiable function $\sigma: \R \to \R$ is called \emph{sigmoidal} if it satisfies

issues.failure_explanation: Definition def:sigm_act demands the limits 0 at -infinity and 1 at +infinity. tanh has limits -1 and 1, and arctan has limits -pi/2 and pi/2. Neither satisfies the definition as stated; only affinely rescaled versions do.

failure_location.quote: the hyperbolic tangens and the arctangens are sigmoidial

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Say that rescaled versions, e.g. (1+tanh)/2 and 1/2+arctan/pi, are sigmoidal, or relax the limit values in the definition.
issues.overall_effect: The list of admissible activations in the scope statement is wrong. The approximation theorems formally apply only to rescaled versions of tanh and arctan.
issues.title: tanh and arctan are not sigmoidal under the paper's own definition
issues.why_classification: A one-line local correction preserves every result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: such that for all $\x \in \mathcal{B}_\rho(\xdag)$ and $\ell =1,\ldots,\no$, the following estimates hold:
the second term in the error estimate \autoref{eq:estimate} seems to be of less importance

issues.failure_explanation: Write A_l(x) for the network approximating <x,x_l> within q, and B_l for the network approximating y_l within r. Then <x,x_l>y_l - A_l B_l = <x,x_l>(y_l - B_l) + (<x,x_l> - A_l)B_l. This is bounded by |<x,x_l>| r + q(||y_l|| + r), which is first order in q and r, not the product q r. For example, with q=0 and N=1 the true error can be |<x,x_1>| r > 0 while the claimed bound N q r is 0. The Remark's conclusion that this term is of little importance is also unsupported. With q and r independent of N, the factor N makes the bound grow.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the term by the correct first-order bound, e.g. N(||x|| r + q(max_l ||y_l|| + r)). Recompute the example rates and the final expression in th:linear.
issues.overall_effect: The estimate rho_n <= nu_N + N q r is invalid. The rates derived from it, 1/(N sqrt(N_j)) and N^{-1-p/2}, are unreliable. The final bound in th:linear, O(sqrt(delta)+sqrt(nu_N+N q r)), is also unreliable.
issues.title: Product-of-errors bound N q r for the network approximation of F^#
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained recomputation. The structure of th:linear in terms of rho_n survives, but the advertised network-size rates change.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: denotes the operator norm of $(I-P_\no)F$, which converges to $0$ when $F$ is compact

issues.failure_explanation: F^# = F P_{X_N}, so Fx - F^#x = F(I-P_{X_N})x. This is not controlled by (I-P_{Y_N})Fx, where P_{Y_N} is the best-approximation projector onto Y_N = F X_N. In fact ||(I-P_{Y_N})F|| <= ||F(I-P_{X_N})||. Counterexample: F=diag(1,eps) on R^2, training image (1,1), x=(1,-1)/sqrt2. Then F^#x=0 and ||Fx-F^#x|| is about 0.707, while ||(I-P_{Y_N})F|| is about 1.41 eps. The factor ||x|| is also missing. Compactness of F alone does not give nu_N -> 0; this needs the training images to be dense so that P_N tends to I strongly.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use ||F(I-P_{X_N})|| (times ||x||) as the truncation term. Add the hypothesis that the training images are asymptotically complete, so that this term tends to 0 for compact F.
issues.overall_effect: The bound rho_n <= nu_N + ... is not justified. The claim that nu_N tends to 0 for compact F is unsupported, so the consistency rho_n -> 0 in th:linear is not established.
issues.title: Truncation error bounded by ||(I-P_N)F|| in the wrong direction, and nu_N -> 0 unjustified
issues.why_classification: The correct quantity and a standard density assumption give a comparable result. The change is contained but needs a new argument and an added hypothesis.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To determine the parameters $w_k$ and $\theta_k$, we solve the implicit equation
If we choose the number of discretization points in the trapezoidal rule to match the number of training data points (i.e., if $N_k=\no$), then we obtain the rate

issues.failure_explanation: The parameters w_k and theta_k are fixed network weights and cannot depend on x. The construction demands sigma(w_k x(t_k)+theta_k) = x(t_k) u(t_k) for all admissible x, i.e. sigma^{-1}(x(t_k)u(t_k)) = w_k x(t_k)+theta_k identically in x. The left side is generally a nonlinear function of x(t_k) and the right side is affine, so no fixed (w_k,theta_k) exists. The 'explicit formula' and the claimed q(N)=N^{-2} are therefore unsupported. In addition, the O(N_k^{-2}) trapezoid constant depends on second derivatives of x u, which are not uniformly bounded over a ball of an L^2-type space, as cor:rate requires.

failure_location.quote: In other words, we get an explicit formula for the coefficients, which can be chosen even independent of $N_l$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a valid one-hidden-layer approximation of the linear functional, for example near-linear sigmoid regimes with a stated error, and restrict to a class of x with uniformly bounded derivatives. Restate q accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed neural functional approximation with rate q(N)=N^{-2}, and the resulting rate estimates and discussion, are not established.
issues.title: Trapezoid example: network coefficients required to depend on x
issues.why_classification: A different construction is needed, giving a possibly different rate. It is contained in an illustrative example and does not change the theory's structure.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note, however, that in general, for nonlinear operator $F$, $\uly^{(\ell)} +\y^{(0)} \neq F[\ulx^{(\ell)}+\x^{(0)}]$.

issues.failure_explanation: For nonlinear F, tilde F_n is built to approximate the linearisation F'[x^(0)] from shifted data, not F. Even a perfect approximation of F' leaves a modelling error of order (L/2)||x-x^(0)||^2 on a fixed ball. Hence ||F-tilde F_n|| <= rho_n with rho_n -> 0 (eq:unifrom, eq:nun) cannot hold for tilde F_n. The hypothesis of thm:added-1 and of the later results is then not met, so these results do not transfer to tilde F_n.

failure_location.quote: results of this and the next section can also be transfer to $\tilde{F}_\n$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the transfer claim, or add an explicit linearisation-error term to rho_n. The latter requires training data in a shrinking neighbourhood of x^dagger and a modified analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The practical link between the training-based construction for nonlinear F and the convergence-rate theory is unsupported.
issues.title: Claim that results transfer to the linearisation-based surrogate for nonlinear F
issues.why_classification: Weakening the claim, or adding an explicit linearisation-error term, is a contained change. The convergence theory itself is unaffected, but the training-based nonlinear construction no longer comes with a rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof follow easily from the Rellich-Kondrachov theorem

issues.failure_explanation: The networks are continuous in the sup-norm, so a uniform approximation on a C-compact set forces F to be sup-norm continuous there. H^s-continuity does not imply this. Counterexample: take V={x_j}∪{0} with x_j=j^{-1}sin(j^{s'}t) scaled so ||x_j||_{H^s}=1 and x_j -> 0 in C. V is C-compact, and any F on V is H^s-continuous because V is discrete in H^s. Set F(x_j)=1 and F(0)=0. No network approximates F within eps<1/2 on V, since F_n(x_j) -> F_n(0). Rellich-Kondrachov gives compactness of the embedding but does not supply sup-norm continuity of F. The same counterexample works for operators.

failure_location.quote: be a continuous functional with respect to the $(H^s(\Omega_\X),\norms{\cdot}_{H^s})$-topology

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require continuity of F with respect to the sup-norm on a C-compact domain, or verify it for the examples. Take D(F) to be a closed H^s-ball intersected with the physical domain. The result then reduces to Tian-Hon.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised extension of universal approximation to Sobolev-space operators is false as stated. th:operatorapx is wrong in the same way.
issues.title: Sobolev 'deviation' of Tian-Hon theorems is not valid (H^s-continuity on a C-compact set)
issues.why_classification: A corrected hypothesis restores a usable approximation theorem for the examples. The claimed generality is lost, but no new architecture is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which is extended by zero outside of $\Omega_\X \subseteq \R^m$

issues.failure_explanation: For the standard nonnegative radial mollifier the Fourier multiplier satisfies phi_hat(xi*zeta)-1 ~ -c xi^2 |zeta|^2 with c>0. Hence ||x_xi-x||_{L^2} ~ c xi^2 ||Δx|| and the order saturates at 2, so xi^{k-s} fails for k-s>2. With zero extension to R^m, a function on a bounded domain that is positive at the boundary has a jump across it. Then ||x_xi-x||_{L^2(Ω)} ~ xi^{1/2}, not xi^2 or even xi^{k-s}. The c-example uses x^dagger>nu>0 in H^2 with this extension and claims O(xi^2).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict (v) to k-s<=2. Replace zero extension by a Sobolev extension operator before mollifying, or assume compact support in the interior. Redo the c-example with the resulting rate.
issues.overall_effect: The mollification rate O(xi^2) for x^dagger_xi - x^dagger, and the xi-dependent rate in the c-example built on it, are unsupported. With plain zero extension the rate is only of order xi^{1/2}.
issues.title: Mollifier approximation rate claimed for all k-s, with zero extension
issues.why_classification: A restricted lemma plus an extension-operator step restores the O(xi^2) rate for the example. The fix is contained but changes the definition of mollification.

issues.failure_explanation: Fréchet differentiability gives only pointwise continuity. Uniformity of ||F[x]-F[x_xi]|| over a ball B_r(x^*) would need sup_x ||x_xi-x||_{L^2} -> 0, which fails: for oscillating x=x^*+r e_k with k >> 1/xi, x_xi is about x^*_xi. The remark's claim ||x_xi-x||=O(xi^2) uniformly on an L^2-neighbourhood is also false, since O(xi^2) requires H^2-regularity. A weaker version holds if r is chosen after eps, using continuity at x^* and ||(x-x^*)_xi||<=||x-x^*||. Then r depends on eps, which conflicts with the fixed-radius use in the rate analysis.

failure_location.quote: it follows that there exists a $\xi > 0$ such that the following holds locally uniformly within an $L^2(\Omega_\X)$-neighborhood

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the estimate via continuity at x^* with radius r=r(eps), or add a regularity or compactness assumption on the neighbourhood. State the rate result with the shrinking radius handled in the Tikhonov analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform L^2-ball estimate rho_{n xi} <= eps on a fixed ball, and the O(rho_{n xi}+xi^2) remark used for the c-example rate, are unsupported.
issues.title: Uniform closeness of F[x] and F[x_xi] over an L^2-ball is not justified
issues.why_classification: A contained argument gives a weaker radius-dependent statement. Using it in the convergence analysis needs extra care but no new overall architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which is extended by zero outside of $\Omega_\X \subseteq \R^m$

issues.failure_explanation: In the c-example D(F)={x>=nu>0}. With zero extension, the mollification of x≡nu has x_xi(0)=nu/2<nu, so x_xi is not in D(F). F[x_xi] and Fréchet differentiability at x_xi are then not covered by the hypotheses. The proof also needs F continuous on the closure of the set of mollified functions, which is not shown to lie in D(F).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume that D(F) is invariant under mollification, or extend F to nonnegative parameters, which is straightforward for the c-example.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's expression F[x]-F_n[x_xi] is not well defined within the stated domain hypothesis, and the proof step is not valid as written.
issues.title: Mollified x_xi need not lie in D(F), so F[x_xi] is undefined
issues.why_classification: A standard domain-extension assumption fixes it without changing the method or result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\xdag > \nu > 0 \in H^2(0,1)$ satisfy the source condition in \autoref{de:source_a}.

issues.failure_explanation: The cited theory yields an error of order sqrt(delta)+sqrt(rho) only for alpha ~ max(delta, rho). Here the effective range error is rho = rho_{n xi}+xi^2, as the paper's own remark says. With alpha~delta, the bound is about sqrt(delta)+xi^2/sqrt(delta), which exceeds the claimed sqrt(delta)+xi whenever xi >> sqrt(delta). The example also invokes the a-example source condition de:source_a rather than de:source_c.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose alpha ~ max(delta, xi^2) and eta ~ alpha^2. Cite de:source_c. The rate O(sqrt(delta)+xi) is then consistent with the remark's argument.
issues.overall_effect: The stated rate O(sqrt(delta)+xi) for the c-example does not follow under the stated parameter choice.
issues.title: c-example parameter choice alpha~delta inconsistent with the xi^2 range error
issues.why_classification: A local parameter correction preserves the stated rate and conclusion.
